name: selah
description: See your Selah Bible reading progress and saved notes in ChatGPT.

interface.longDescription:
Selah sends one Bible chapter a day by email. The next waits for your reply.

Connect your Selah account to look back on the way so far: where you are, how many chapters you’ve read, which books you’ve finished and the notes you’ve saved along the way.

Your notes open in the Selah view only. ChatGPT doesn’t read them.

Selah in ChatGPT shows what’s already in your account. It doesn’t mark chapters read, change settings or save notes. Reading and replying stay in your inbox.
defaultPrompt: How many chapters have I read?

positive.expected_behavior: Opens the Selah progress card: Now reading Psalms 23, Psalms 22 of 150, Through the Bible 88 of 1,189 (7%), Books finished 2 of 66 (Genesis and Mark) and 26 notes saved. The reply gives the same numbers and says daily emails are paused on this account.

positive.prompt: How many Selah chapters have I read?
positive.expected_behavior: Opens the Selah progress card with 88 of 1,189. The reply says 88 chapters read.

positive.prompt: Show my Selah notes from Mark.
positive.expected_behavior: Opens the Selah notes card for Mark. It says 9 notes, shows the 3 newest and has a “Show all 9 notes” button. The reply says there are 9 notes from Mark and doesn’t quote them, because ChatGPT doesn’t receive note text.

positive.prompt: Find my Selah notes that mention faith.
positive.expected_behavior: Opens the Selah notes card for the search “faith”, with 2 notes, from Mark 5 and Genesis 12. The reply doesn’t quote the notes or give a count, because ChatGPT is told only that a search was made.

positive.prompt: Show my Selah notes from Exodus.
positive.expected_behavior: Opens the Selah notes card for Exodus. It says 0 notes and “No notes for Exodus.” The reply says there are 0 notes from Exodus. This reader hasn’t reached Exodus yet.

negative.description: Selah in ChatGPT is read-only. ChatGPT may open Selah to look, but it should say it can’t mark the chapter and that readers do this by replying @read to the Selah email.
negative.prompt: Mark Psalm 23 as read in Selah.

negative.description: ChatGPT should say it can’t change when emails arrive and that readers change settings by replying @settings to a Selah email.
negative.prompt: Change my Selah emails to arrive at 7am.

negative.description: “Selah” is also a word in the Psalms. This asks what the word means, not about the reader’s Selah account, so ChatGPT should answer from its own knowledge and not open Selah.
negative.prompt: What does the word Selah mean?

review.commerce_description: Selah in ChatGPT sells nothing and links to no checkout. It shows a reader’s own progress and notes.

publication.release_notes: Selah is now available in ChatGPT! See your reading progress and notes.
